Prepared for Coinbase listing and integration reviewers, 2026-10-22.
Companion documents: the [integration plan](/listings/coinbase/integration-plan/) and the
[comparisons with XRP, Zcash and post-quantum chains](/listings/coinbase/comparisons/).

## 1. Purpose

This guide tells an AI agent how to review Post Fiat L1 (PFTL, repository
`postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2`) the way an exchange's integration and security
reviewers would. It covers:

- the rules the agent must follow;
- the order in which to read the repository, and what to extract from each
  file;
- a map of every crate;
- commands that test the claims an exchange cares about, with the results
  observed on 2026-10-22;
- a checklist that maps PFTL evidence onto Coinbase's Digital Asset Security
  Assessment Framework (DASAF);
- contradictions already found, and questions to put to the Post Fiat team.

The agent's job is to establish what is true at a pinned commit and to say
plainly what is not established. Its job is not to argue for a listing.

**Starting facts.** PFTL runs as `postfiat-wan-devnet-2`, a devnet of six
validators that the Post Fiat Foundation administers
([chain-state-current.md:571-572](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/docs/status/chain-state-current.md);
[whitepaper.md:162](/whitepaper/)). The repository calls it a "closed
controlled devnet" that outsiders cannot yet join as validators
([public-operator-runbook.md:12-13](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/docs/runbooks/public-operator-runbook.md)).
There is no mainnet. The code has not been externally audited
([SECURITY.md:27-31](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/SECURITY.md)).

## 2. Ground rules

1. **The repository is the source of truth.** Record the commit you review
   (`git rev-parse HEAD`) at the top of your report. This guide's line
   numbers refer to `ac7a49822`, the head of `main` on the morning of 2026-10-22. The five later commits on `main` (through `a2516a1b8`) change storage-evidence tooling, plans and handoffs only, not `crates/`, `third_party/` or Cargo files, so code line references still hold. If your commit differs,
   re-locate each reference with `grep -n` before you cite it.
2. **Cite `file:line` for every claim.** Use paths relative to the
   repository root. For a range, cite the first and last line. A claim with
   no citation is an opinion and must be labelled as one.
3. **Prefer code over documents.** When a document and the code disagree,
   report the disagreement with both locations, state what the code does, and
   say which document is stale. Section 7 lists disagreements already found.
4. **Keep four kinds of status apart:**
   - *in source*: a commit exists;
   - *deployed*: the commit is an ancestor of the release recorded in
     [chain-state-current.md](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/docs/status/chain-state-current.md);
   - *activated*: a consensus rule is live at a recorded height;
   - *demonstrated*: a retained, project-authored record exists. The
     whitepaper says "neither word means independently audited"
     ([whitepaper.md:17](/whitepaper/)).

   To test whether a fix is deployed, run
   `git merge-base --is-ancestor <fix-commit> <release-source-commit>`.
5. **Project-authored evidence is not independent evidence.** Reports under
   `reports/`, `benchmarks/` and `deployments/` were produced by the project.
   Describe them as such.
6. **Point-in-time state is not current state.** `chain-state-current.md` is
   a log of observations with timestamps. Quote the timestamp. A current Git
   HEAD is not deployment evidence ([cobalt.md:48-49](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/docs/governance/cobalt.md)).
7. **Do not touch live systems or keys.** Use read-only RPC only. Do not
   submit transactions, request faucet funds or handle key files. Do not
   commit, push or edit repository files.
8. **Keep the worktree clean.** Set `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` outside the
   repository. Do not run anything that writes `Cargo.lock` files into
   excluded workspaces (`third_party/*`, `tools/*`, `programs/*`). Copy them
   to a temporary directory first.
9. **Keep test scope proportional.** Orchard and Asset-Orchard proving tests
   are release-scale (minutes each). Run them only when the claim needs them
   ([AGENTS.md, "Keep test scope proportional"](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/AGENTS.md)).
10. **Cite external facts with URLs.** Mark anything you could not confirm.
    Several Coinbase and EUR-Lex pages block automated fetches; say so rather
    than guess.

## 4. Crate map

The root [Cargo.toml](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/Cargo.toml) lists 28 workspace members. Two
more directories under `crates/` are Foundry (Solidity) packages, not Rust
crates. `programs/*`, `tools/*` and `third_party/fips204` are excluded from
the workspace. `third_party/halo2_proofs` replaces crates.io `halo2_proofs`
through `[patch.crates-io]`.

| Directory | Package | What it is | Notable targets |
|---|---|---|---|
| `arc-conformance` | `arc-conformance` | Golden-fixture checks for the Arc testnet (chain 5,042,002): Ed25519 commit certificates, validator registry, receipt-trie proofs. Its `address_from_public_key` derives EVM addresses, not PFTL addresses. | bins `capture`, `capture_receipts` |
| `arc-sp1-contracts` | — (Foundry) | Pins the SP1 v6.1.0 Groth16 verifier and gateway for Arc (solc 0.8.20). | `test/`, `script/` |
| `bench_harness` | `postfiat-bench` | Internal benchmark and acceptance harness: ML-DSA signing, ordering, execution, storage, bridge. | `postfiat-bench`, `postfiat-storage-corpus-batches` |
| `bridge` | `postfiat-bridge` | Bridge state machine, witness attestations, Ethereum receipt and checkpoint verification. | — |
| `cobalt_adversarial_oracle` | `postfiat-cobalt-adversarial-oracle` | Second, independent Cobalt E1 oracle and corpus generator; depends on no PFTL crate. | bin of the same name |
| `cobalt_decision_oracle` | `postfiat-cobalt-decision-oracle` | Independent oracle for Cobalt activation and retirement decisions. | bin of the same name |
| `cobalt_e1_harness` | `postfiat-cobalt-e1-harness` | Cross-checks both oracles against production Cobalt. | bin |
| `cobalt_e2_harness` | `postfiat-cobalt-e2-harness` | Byzantine-validator campaign (E2). | bin |
| `cobalt_e3_harness` | `postfiat-cobalt-e3-harness` | Adversarial durable-recovery campaign (E3). | bin |
| `consensus_cobalt` | `postfiat-consensus-cobalt` | Cobalt: essential subsets, trust graphs, RBC/ABBA/MVBA, DABC ratification, validator-admission policy, cover extractor. | 24 examples (14 need `cobalt-unsafe-simulation`); test `genesis_registry_checker` |
| `crypto_provider` | `postfiat-crypto-provider` | ML-DSA-65 wrappers over vendored `fips204`; signing contexts; SHA3-384 domain hashing; address derivation. | example `ml_dsa_budget`; features `mldsa-guest-acceleration`, `sp1-cycle-tracking` |
| `ethereum-contracts` | — (Foundry) | Solidity 0.8.24 contracts: bridge vaults, PFTL finality and withdrawal verifiers, Uniswap primary market, mint controller, NAV guard. | 24 test files |
| `execution` | `postfiat-execution` | Deterministic state transition and receipts: fees, reserve, transfers, `payment_v2`, issued assets, NAV, SP1 Groth16 verification. | — |
| `fastpay-prototype` | `postfiat-fastpay-prototype` | Research prototype of FastPay owned-object payments with 2f+1 certificates. | `fastpay-m1-bench`, `fastpay-flow` |
| `fastswap_model` | `postfiat-fastswap-model` | Explicit-state safety model of FastSwap v1. | `fastswap-model-check` |
| `fuzz_harness` | `postfiat-fuzz` | Adversarial and fuzz targets, including `native-supply-invariants`. | `postfiat-fuzz` |
| `mempool_dag` | `postfiat-mempool-dag` | DAG batch dissemination and payload availability (1 MiB / 1,024 transactions per batch). | — |
| `nav_reserve_protocol` | `postfiat-nav-reserve-protocol` | Host-side construction of NAV reserve packets and composite source roots. | — |
| `network` | `postfiat-network` | Bounded validator networking, message framing, fault plans. | — |
| `node` | `postfiat-node` | Validator node, RPC server, CLI, wallet flows, Orchard actions, Cobalt handoff, storage commit. | bins `postfiat-node` ([Cargo.toml:13-15](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/crates/node/Cargo.toml)), `asset-orchard-local-service`, six `postfiat-cobalt-*` tools, `pftl_swapd`, `pftl_swapctl` and others; integration tests `atomic_swap_local_six`, `fastpay_default_rpc`, `fastswap_local_six`, `wallet_test_vector_redaction` |

| `pftl_uniswap_proofs` | `postfiat-pftl-uniswap-proofs` | Proof statement for finalized PFTL-to-Uniswap primary-mint receipts. | — |
| `pfusdc_proofs` | `postfiat-pfusdc-proofs` | Tier-4 pfUSDC proof-statement verification. | — |

Outside `crates/`, the reviewer will also meet:
- `tools/nav-reserve-proof`, the reserve-proof kit;
- `programs/pfusdc-*` and `programs/pftl-uniswap-receipt`, the SP1 guests;
- `python/postfiat_rpc`, the Python RPC client and operator CLIs;
- `wallet-web` and `wallet-extension`, the wallets.

## 5. How to verify the key claims

**Setup.** The toolchain is pinned to Rust 1.95.0
([rust-toolchain.toml](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/rust-toolchain.toml)). Run from the
repository root:

```bash
export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/pftl-review-target   # keep target/ out of the worktree
git rev-parse HEAD
```

The results below were observed on 2026-10-22 at `ac7a49822` on a 32-core
host with a warm Cargo registry. A cold build takes longer. Every test listed
passed.

### 5.1 Signatures, addresses and the transaction envelope

| Claim | Command | Observed result | Code |
|---|---|---|---|

### 5.7 Whole-workspace and deployment checks

- **CI battery.** `cargo test --workspace --locked`
  ([.github/workflows/rust-ci.yml:47-52](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/.github/workflows/rust-ci.yml)).
  Long; run it once, last. For this guide the full lib suites of
  `postfiat-types` (151 tests), `postfiat-execution` (216),
  `postfiat-ordering-fast` (35), `postfiat-consensus-cobalt` (75) and
  `postfiat-rpc-sdk` (191) passed. The full `postfiat-node` lib suite (434
  tests) had not finished after 13 minutes in a debug build and was stopped;
  only the filtered node tests listed above were run to completion.
- **Deployed fixes.** For each fix you rely on, run
  `git merge-base --is-ancestor <fix> 86706699`. `86706699` is the source of
  release `store-handle-20261021`, deployed to all six validators on
  2026-10-21 ([chain-state-current.md:3-20](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/docs/status/chain-state-current.md)).
  `e95efbdf`, `c9a61fcd`, `f2dea308`, `f9f13ead`, `8644f0af` and `15af691d`
  all pass this check.
- **Following the chain** (needs RPC access from the team):
  `postfiat-node rpc-catch-up-certified-delta --expected-height N
  --expected-block-hash H --expected-state-root R`, then compare `status`
  across endpoints
  ([public-operator-runbook.md:175-211](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/docs/runbooks/public-operator-runbook.md)).

## 6. Checklist against Coinbase's assessment framework

Coinbase's Digital Asset Security Assessment Framework has five review
categories:

- **Vulnerabilities:** "Known vulnerabilities have been remediated."
- **Transaction Finality & Balance Certainty:** "The ability to determine
  when transactions are effectively finalized."
- **Trustless Node Operation:** "Open access to independently verify the
  legitimacy of network operations."
- **Coinbase Compatibility:** "The asset's compatibility with Coinbase
  systems."
- **Support:** "Sufficient support from the asset issuer available."

A critical risk fails a review on its own. Coinbase's worked example is a
"central authority" that can "arbitrarily control block production"
([Coinbase, 2022-11-29](https://www.coinbase.com/blog/reviewing-blockchain-designs-to-determine-confidence-in-custodiability)).

### 6.1 Vulnerabilities

| Check | PFTL evidence | Known gaps |
|---|---|---|
| External audit | None ([SECURITY.md:27-31](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/SECURITY.md)) | Specialist reviews of consensus, circuits, contracts and bridge are open ([release gates](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/docs/status/release-gate-inventory.md) rows 11–14). |
| Internal defect tracking | [Defect inventory](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/docs/review/defect-inventory-20260910.md): 142 rows. By its status column, 20 of 27 P1 rows are fixed or closed. | Open or only dispositioned P1 rows include SH-03 (wallet keys or note openings copied to validators; cleanup not guaranteed on SIGKILL or compromise) and SH-10 (release-ID reuse before aggregate verification). Recount: the parse is approximate. |
| Cryptographic dependencies | [Cryptography inventory](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/docs/status/OPEN-SOURCE-CRYPTOGRAPHY-INVENTORY-20260716.md); Orchard advisory handled ([comparisons §2.3](/listings/coinbase/comparisons/#23-the-2026-orchard-soundness-bug-and-what-it-means-for-pftl)) | Replay verifying keys of unknown provenance; Orchard 0.15 migration deadline in [deny.toml:14](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/deny.toml) has passed. |
| Consensus safety | Cross-phase round floor in code with regressions (section 5.3) | No progress (liveness) theorem ([whitepaper.md:197](/whitepaper/)). |
| Reserve proofs | [Mechanics review](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/docs/review/nav-reserve-proof-mechanics-review-20260924.md): three P1 findings | G1 unfixed for A666; PR #49 open. Relevant to NAVCoins, not to native PFT custody. |
| Dependency policy | [deny.toml](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/deny.toml); `cargo-deny` in CI ([product-security-ci.yml:64](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/.github/workflows/product-security-ci.yml)) | Review each advisory ignore and its reason. |

### 6.2 Transaction finality and balance certainty

| Check | PFTL evidence | Known gaps |
|---|---|---|
| Deterministic finality | Commit QC from `q` distinct ML-DSA-65 precommits; no fork choice ([finality.md](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/docs/architecture/finality.md)) | The client must also check the receipt code; certified blocks can hold rejected transactions. |
| **Central authority (critical)** | Six validators, all Foundation-administered ([whitepaper.md:162](/whitepaper/)); Cobalt governs validator trust only ([cobalt.md](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/docs/governance/cobalt.md)) | **Fails today on this criterion.** E6 independent-operator gate open; release gates 18 and 20 open. |
| Who can move or burn others' funds | No native-PFT clawback or mint path ([native supply inventory](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/docs/status/OPEN-SOURCE-NATIVE-SUPPLY-INVENTORY-20260716.md)). Issued assets support issuer-declared clawback (`asset_clawback`, [core_chain.rs:22](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/crates/types/src/core_chain.rs)). | The Foundation "retains authority over unrelated governance scopes" ([whitepaper.md:195](/whitepaper/)). Enumerate every governance action (Orchard pause and resume, NAV halt, route pause, FastPay and FastSwap committee changes) and state for each whether it can freeze or move a user's native PFT. |
| History immutability | "No authority can retroactively alter certificate thresholds"; returning authority "cannot rewrite finalized history" ([whitepaper.md:195](/whitepaper/); [cobalt.md:24-25](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/docs/governance/cobalt.md)) | Verify against [cobalt_handoff.rs](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/crates/node/src/cobalt_handoff.rs). |
| Supply certainty | Genesis-only creation; per-block replay invariant (section 5.2) | Production supply and decimals not fixed in code (C7). |
| Liveness | Loss of quorum halts rather than weakening `q` | Recorded stalls: [postmortems](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/docs/postmortems/devnet-registry-continuation-wedge-2026-08-31.md); [FastPay view-change issue](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/docs/status/fastpay-effect-anchoring-fix-20260928.md). |

### 6.3 Trustless node operation

| Check | PFTL evidence | Known gaps |
|---|---|---|
| Open source, buildable | Public repository; pinned toolchain; `--locked` builds | Second-builder reproduction of release hashes is open (release gate 7). |
| Independent verification of history | Committed blocks embed the proposal and both QCs; full replay is "an out-of-band audit path" ([finality.md:21-24, 98-99](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/docs/architecture/finality.md)); `rpc-catch-up-certified-delta`, `archive-window-verify` ([operator runbook](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/docs/runbooks/public-operator-runbook.md)) | Outsiders cannot join today ([operator runbook:10-19](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/docs/runbooks/public-operator-runbook.md)); public operator runbook gate open (row 19). Ask whether Coinbase can run a non-validating follower against the devnet. |
| History retention | Full-archive, retained and pruned roles ([state-and-storage.md](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/docs/architecture/state-and-storage.md)) | Confirm who runs a full archive, and how a new node obtains full history. |
| RPC exposure | Public RPC only behind an authenticated TLS edge; plaintext public binds rejected ([SECURITY.md:67-68](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/SECURITY.md)) | Write methods are "controlled" ([rpc/methods.md](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/docs/rpc/methods.md)). |

### 6.4 Coinbase compatibility

| Check | PFTL evidence | Known gaps |
|---|---|---|
| Signing | ML-DSA-65 with FIPS 204 context `postfiat-l1-v2/tx/v1` ([crypto_provider/src/lib.rs:16](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/crates/crypto_provider/src/lib.rs)); Mesh has an `ml_dsa_65` curve type ([PR #129](https://github.com/coinbase/mesh-specifications/pull/129)) | Coinbase custody's post-quantum signing pipeline is planned "within the next year" ([Coinbase blog](https://www.coinbase.com/blog/what-coinbase-is-doing-to-prepare-for-post-quantum-cryptography)). No HSM or external-signer interface in PFTL ([custody model](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/docs/specs/wallet-exchange-custody-model.md)). |
| Integration API | JSON RPC and Rust/Python SDKs ([rpc_sdk](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/crates/rpc_sdk/src/lib.rs); [python/postfiat_rpc](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/python/postfiat_rpc/client.py)) | No Mesh implementation in the repository. |
| Address safety | Wallets check `^pf[0-9a-f]{40}$` ([popup.js:277](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/wallet-extension/popup/popup.js)) | No checksum; protocol does not validate recipient format (section 5.1). |
| Deposit attribution | Per-customer addresses; `payment_v2` memos | No require-memo flag. `account_tx` rows carry only `memo_hash` and `memo_count` ([block_finality.rs:1009-1010](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/crates/node/src/block_finality.rs)) and list only transparent kinds ([account-history.md](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/docs/rpc/account-history.md)); shielded withdrawals and owned-object lanes need separate checks. |
| Key management | Deterministic seed derivation including chain ID ([wallet_sdk.rs:1078-1107](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/crates/rpc_sdk/src/wallet_sdk.rs)) | No BIP32 or xpub; no account key rotation; no multi-signing. |
| Transaction lifecycle | Strict next-sequence; duplicate pending sequence rejected at admission ([envelope spec](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/docs/specs/transparent-transaction-envelope.md)) | v1 envelope has no expiry. Ask how a stuck or unwanted pending transaction is cleared. |
| Units | 1 PFT = 1,000,000 atoms in wallets ([utils.js:11-12](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/wallet-web/src/lib/utils.js)) | Not a protocol constant. |

### 6.5 Support

| Check | PFTL evidence | Known gaps |
|---|---|---|
| Security intake | GitHub private advisory only; acknowledgement within 72 hours ([SECURITY.md:5-20](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/SECURITY.md)) | No email or PGP fallback. Only the latest `main` is supported (`:22-25`). |
| Documentation | Extensive `docs/`, published with MkDocs ([mkdocs.yml](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/mkdocs.yml)) | Several documents are stale (section 7). |
| Release discipline | [release-process.md](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/docs/release-process.md); signed manifests; one-validator-at-a-time rollouts logged in [chain-state-current.md](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/docs/status/chain-state-current.md) | Per-release gates 6–8 and 10 have no public-testnet receipt yet. |
| Incident handling | [incident-response.md](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/docs/runbooks/incident-response.md); postmortems | No external status feed. |
| Contributor base | `git shortlog -sn --since=2026-07-17 HEAD`: 1,630 of 1,867 public commits come from one author identity | Concentration risk; public history starts on 2026-07-17 (`11839c14f`). |

## 8. Open questions for the Post Fiat team

1. **Production genesis.** What are the total supply, decimals, chain ID and
   initial validator set, and when do independent operators join? Which
   operators, under what agreements?
2. **Governance reach.** List every governance action outside Cobalt's
   validator-trust scope. Can any of them freeze, move, burn or revert native
   PFT held by a third party?
3. **Addresses.** What is the design and timeline for a checksummed address
   and for rejecting malformed recipients at admission and in execution?
4. **Attribution.** Will there be a require-memo (`RequireDest`-style) flag?
   Is memo-based attribution intended for exchanges? `account_tx` returns only
   `memo_hash` and `memo_count`
   ([block_finality.rs:1009-1010](https://github.com/postfiatorg/postfiatl1v2/blob/e067eb719ae41301d8e0421d7220406af838260b/crates/node/src/block_finality.rs));
   which read method returns the memo bytes?
5. **History completeness.** Which lanes can credit a transparent address
   (Orchard withdrawal, FastPay unwrap, FastLane exit, atomic swap legs, NAV
   redemption settlement)? Which of them appear in `account_tx`?
6. **Node access.** Can Coinbase run a non-validating follower or archive
   node against `postfiat-wan-devnet-2` now? Which endpoints, and what
   retention?
7. **Signing.** Will the protocol accept externally generated ML-DSA-65 keys
   and signatures from an HSM that supports FIPS 204 context strings? Is an
   account key-rotation transaction planned?
8. **Pending transactions.** With no expiry in the envelope, how does a
   custodian cancel or replace a transaction that is stuck in the mempool?
9. **Audits.** What are the scope, firm and timeline for audits of
   consensus, Cobalt, the Asset-Orchard circuits (`h_action`, gate P13), the
   SP1 guests and the Ethereum contracts?
10. **Orchard history.** Which circuit versions produced the proofs that the
    replay verifying keys check? Were any pre-fix (unanchored) proofs
    accepted on the devnet? What is the Orchard 0.15 plan?
11. **Consensus.** Are the consensus-affecting fixes in the deployed release
    active? When will the whitepaper's §1.9 be updated?
12. **NAVCoins.** When will A666 move off `sp1-groth16` (G1)? Will PR #49 be
    adopted?
13. **Legal.** Will counsel's opinion on MiCA Article 76(3) and AMLR Article
    79 be shared ([comparisons §2.5](/listings/coinbase/comparisons/#25-eu-rules-questions-for-counsel))?

## 9. Report template

Structure the agent's output as follows.

1. **Commit reviewed** and date. **Deployed release** and source commit,
   quoted from `chain-state-current.md` with its timestamp.
2. **Summary.** One paragraph per DASAF category: pass, fail or not
   established, with the deciding evidence.
3. **Findings.** For each: ID; severity (critical or non-critical in DASAF
   terms); the claim; evidence (`file:line`, command and output); and what
   would resolve it.
4. **Contradictions.** Section 7 rows confirmed, refuted or newly found.
5. **Commands run.** Exact commands, exit status, test counts, wall time.
6. **Not verified.** Everything the agent could not check, and why.
7. **Questions for the team.**
